title: Bursfelde Benedictine missal: bounded 1498 and 1518 book states

traditions.label: Bursfelde Benedictine observance
traditions.scope: The printed missal expressly assigned to the Bursfelde union and observance, without treating other Benedictine congregations as one recension.
traditions.coverage_note: Original leaves establish scoped 1498 and 1518 book witnesses and a documented witness succession described by the 1518 printing itself. Chapter authorization, house reception, wider text and the relation to 1481 and 1534 prints remain open.

sources.title: Missale ordinis sancti Benedicti, BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 3665 s
sources.inspection: Original BSB scan images 3 (title), 6 (Trithemius letter) and 19 (fol. 1r temporal Mass opening) visually inspected on 2026-10-20; the IIIF manifest identifies the 604-canvas object, shelfmark, printer and bracketed publication date. On 2026-10-21 further original images were inspected: image 6 (Trithemius letter heading and opening: correction of this missal in orthography, e.g. iesus/ioannes without and Christus with aspiration), image 7 (January calendar) and images 331–332 (Te igitur through the Communicantes apostle list).
sources.limitations: Only selected leaves were read (images 3, 6, 7, 19, 331–332). The dated colophon and full Mass Ordinary, Canon, calendar and rubrics were not inspected. The scan manifest carries a Public Domain Mark; no historical text or image is republished here.

sources.title: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek IIIF manifest for bsb00030079
sources.inspection: Manifest metadata read on 2026-10-20: title Missale Benedictinum Bursfeldense; Speyer, Peter Drach; bracketed 1498-07-30 date; call number 2 Inc.c.a. 3665 s; 604 canvases; prefatory letter dated 1497-08-05.
sources.limitations: The manifest's date is catalogue metadata. Its transcription of the colophon was not checked against that leaf.

sources.title: USUARIUM 220, Missale Romano-Bursfeldense
sources.inspection: Full book record and contents index read on 2026-10-20; identifies the 1498 Speyer Bursfelde copy and indexed temporal, Ordinary, Canon, sanctoral, common, votive and rubrical sections.
sources.limitations: The contents index is not page-level collation. It labels image 6 a decree, but the image is a prefatory letter. USUARIUM requests attribution for use of its dataset.

sources.title: USUARIUM 469, Missale Benedictinum
sources.inspection: Full book record read on 2026-10-20: distinct 1481 Bamberg Johannes Sensenschmidt printing, OSB (IT), BSB 2 L.impr.membr. 71, Weale-Bohatta 1680.
sources.limitations: Original 1481 leaves and any textual relation to the 1498 Bursfelde print were not inspected; the catalogue identity alone proves no ancestry. USUARIUM requests attribution for use of its dataset.

sources.title: Missale denuo diligentissime castigatum et revisum Ordinis sancti Benedicti reformatorum nigrorum monachorum Bursfeldensium, Hagenau: Thomas Anshelm, 1518; BSB Res/2 Liturg. 451 q
sources.inspection: Original BSB IIIF images inspected on 2026-10-21: image 7 title; image 12 recognitor's letter (letter of the book's unnamed recognitor to the Benedictine professors throughout Germany, commending the printer Thomas Anshelm of Baden; dated 1518 under Leo X and Maximilian); image 13 January calendar; images 319–320 Te igitur through the Communicantes apostle list; image 559 red colophon (Hagenau, according to the rite and custom of the Benedictine observance throughout Germany, Thomas Anshelm, January 1518, from an exemplar newly emended and corrected in many places by a religious of the same order). Manuscript supplements on images 5–6 and 8 were viewed.
sources.limitations: Selected leaves only; no complete-book collation. The letter is a printer's address to the order's monks, not a chapter authorization. The handwritten additions are copy-specific and undated, and the owning house is not identified from the inspected images. Images retained only in scratch.

sources.title: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek IIIF manifest for bsb10197473
sources.inspection: Manifest metadata read on 2026-10-21: title as on the title leaf; Hagenoie: Anßhelmus; date 1518; extent [12], CXXXIIII, [20] leaves; VD16 M 5641; call number Res/2 Liturg. 451 q; 566 canvases.
sources.limitations: Catalogue metadata; the colophon month was read separately from the original image.

sources.title: Missale Benedictinum, Bamberg: Johann Sensenschmidt, 31 July 1481; BSB 2 L.impr.membr. 71
sources.inspection: BSB manifest metadata (Bamberg, Johann Sensenschmidt, 1481.07.31, GW M24117, 262 leaves, 521 canvases) and original images 287–288 (Te igitur intercession list through the Communicantes apostle list, printed fol. CXLIII on 288) inspected on 2026-10-21.
sources.limitations: Only the two Canon openings were read; title, colophon, calendar and propers uninspected. USUARIUM 469 labels this printing Italian OSB, while the BSB imprint is Bamberg; no Bursfelde assignment or ancestry is inferred.

stages.label: 1498 Bursfelde observance missal
stages.date_label: 1498 Speyer printing; exact colophon date unverified
stages.scope: The inspected title and fol. 1r First Sunday of Advent Mass opening identify the printed temporal as according to the Bursfelde union and observance. The indexed whole-book contents are a finding aid, not a collated text. Further inspected units: the Canon's Te igitur intercession list and Memento (images 331–332) and the January calendar (image 7).
stages.witness_label: Missale ordinis sancti Benedicti, Speyer, Peter Drach, 1498; BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 3665 s
stages.summary: The first temporal Mass opening names the Bursfelde union and observance and gives the First Sunday of Advent formulary. This identifies a local Benedictine book state, with no claim that the book revises the 1481 Benedictine printing.

evidence.locus: BSB image 3, title; image 19, fol. 1r, red temporal heading and First Advent opening
evidence.claim: Original leaves identify a Benedictine missal whose temporal is assigned to the Bursfelde union and observance.

evidence.locus: Title, Published, Date and Call number metadata
evidence.claim: The library identifies the Speyer Peter Drach printing as 1498 and its copy as 2 Inc.c.a. 3665 s.

evidence.locus: Book 220 metadata and contents list, pp. 3, 19, 307, 331, 349, 409, 456 and 566
evidence.claim: The index connects the inspected copy to a complete Missal with identifiable Mass components.

evidence.locus: BSB images 331–332, Te igitur and Memento; image 7, January calendar; image 6, Trithemius letter
evidence.claim: Te igitur names papa nostro N., antistite nostro N. and rege nostro N. (a red stroke cancels the et before rege in this copy); the Memento includes pro quibus tibi offerimus vel; the January calendar lists, among others, Commemoratio abbatum (7 Jan.), Maurus abbas with twelve lessons (15 Jan.) and Conversio Pauli duplex minus. Trithemius describes chiefly orthographic correction of this missal, with some named textual emendations in the readings (e.g. the Johannine Passion).

stages.limitations: The 1497 Trithemius leaf is a prefatory letter, not an inspected promulgation. The exact 1498 colophon leaf, general chapter authorization, full text, and differences from other Benedictine books are unexamined. The 1481 USUARIUM 469 printing is a distinct bibliographic witness, not an established predecessor. The Trithemius letter describes chiefly orthographic correction, with some named textual emendations in the readings (e.g. the Johannine Passion), not a liturgical revision.
stages.reception: The printed heading states intended Bursfelde use; actual celebration from this edition at any named house and uniform adoption throughout the union are not established.

stages.label: 1518 Hagenau re-emended Bursfelde missal
stages.scope: Title, recognitor's letter, colophon, January calendar and the Canon's Te igitur and Memento of the Hagenau 1518 printing for the Bursfelde observance; selected leaves, not a collated book.
stages.witness_label: Missale ... Ordinis sancti Benedicti reformatorum nigrorum monachorum Bursfeldensium, Hagenau, Thomas Anshelm, 1518; BSB Res/2 Liturg. 451 q
stages.summary: The title calls the book newly and most diligently corrected and revised for the reformed black monks of Bursfelde. The printer's recognitor says the order's missals had been carefully emended by Johannes Trithemius in orthography and accents but had since become corrupted by copyists, and that this edition expunges those faults; the colophon calls its exemplar newly emended and corrected in many places by a religious of the order. The inspected Canon units and the January feast entries agree in content with the 1498 printing; the January golden numbers differ.

evidence.claim: Missale denuo diligentissime castigatum et revisum Ordinis sancti Benedicti reformatorum nigrorum monachorum Bursfeldensium.

The letter names Trithemius's earlier emendation of the order's missals in orthography and accents, reports later corruption, describes this revision as removing faults, and is dated 1518 under Leo X and Maximilian.
Printed at Hagenau by Thomas Anshelm in January 1518 according to the rite and custom of the Benedictine observance in Germany, from an exemplar newly emended by a religious of the order.

evidence.locus: BSB images 319–320, Te igitur to Communicantes; image 13, January calendar
evidence.claim: Te igitur names papa nostro N., antistite nostro N. and rege nostro N.; the Memento includes pro quibus tibi offerimus vel; the January feast entries correspond to the 1498 calendar; the golden-number column differs.

evidence.locus: Title, Published, Date, Extent, VD16 and Call number metadata
evidence.claim: The library identifies the Hagenau Anshelm printing of 1518, VD16 M 5641.

stages.limitations: Selected leaves only. The recognitor's account describes correction of copying and orthographic faults; it does not identify specific liturgical changes, and none were found in the sampled units. Neither the letter nor the colophon is a chapter authorization. The relationship to the catalogue-reported 1534 printing is unexamined.
stages.reception: The book is addressed to Benedictine professors throughout Germany and assigned to the Bursfelde observance. This BSB copy carries undated manuscript Mass-proper supplements for saints venerated at Trier (among them Eucharius, Valerius, Maternus, Agritius, Celsus and Matthias, including an Electio sancti Mathie entry and a Matthias sequence), which show local supplementation in one copy; the house and date of use are not identified.

transitions.summary: The 1518 printing describes itself as a re-emendation of the Trithemius-corrected Bursfelde missal text, removing faults introduced since; the sampled Canon units agree in content, and the January feasts, grades and dating agree while its golden-number column is reset. No substantive liturgical revision is documented.

evidence.locus: BSB image 12, recognitor's letter; image 559, colophon
evidence.claim: Primary description: the base is the order's missal as emended by Trithemius in orthography and accents; the new exemplar was emended again and corrected in many places.
The 1498 printing carries Trithemius's letter describing his orthographic correction of this missal.
1498 January calendar and Canon openings read for the comparison.

1518 Canon openings agree in content with 1498 apart from spelling and typesetting (for example circumastantium); the January feast entries agree, but the golden-number column differs (1498 iii at 1 Jan., xi at 3, xix at 5; 1518 begins v at 5, xiii at 6, ii at 8, the series set four days earlier).

transitions.limitations: Bounded comparison of the Te igitur, Memento, opening Communicantes and January calendar only. The recognitor names Trithemius's emended missal books, not the exact 1498 Speyer copy, as the text he revised, so parentage is attributed rather than established. Agreement in sampled units does not prove agreement elsewhere. The January golden numbers were reset; other months and the purpose of the change were not examined, and it is not recorded as a liturgical change.

gaps.missing: Bursfelde chapter or other competent authorization and dated evidence of use of the 1498 printing at named houses. The 1518 successor carries only a printer's recognitor letter and colophon, not an authorization; its BSB copy has undated manuscript supplements for Trier saints without an identified house.
gaps.next_source: Bursfelde chapter recesses (BSB Clm 4406 covers chapters 1417–1485 only, before this printing) and later recesses, ownership or use annotations, house inventories and accounts alongside the original prefatory leaves; identify the house behind the Trier-saint supplements in BSB Res/2 Liturg. 451 q.
gaps.consequence: The stage is a scoped book attestation, not an act-history station or proof of union-wide adoption.

gaps.missing: Collated component differences among the 1481 Bamberg Benedictine print, the 1498 Speyer and 1518 Hagenau Bursfelde prints and the catalogue-reported 1534 Bursfelde printing beyond the sampled units. On 2026-10-21 the Te igitur intercession list, Memento and opening Communicantes were found to agree in content in 1481 (BSB bsb00030076 images 287–288), 1498 (bsb00030079 images 331–332) and 1518 (bsb10197473 images 319–320), and the 1498 and 1518 January calendars agree in feasts and grades but not in their golden-number columns; the 1518 recognitor describes only correction of copying and orthographic faults.
gaps.next_source: Compare the 1498 and 1518 Ordinary, prefaces, temporal and sanctoral formularies and the remaining calendar months; identify an original of the 1534 printing (it was not found in the BSB digital collections searched on 2026-10-21) and inspect the 1481 title, colophon and calendar.
gaps.consequence: A documented 1498→1518 witness succession rests on the 1518 printing's own description and sampled agreement. No substantive revision, and no relation of either print to 1481 or 1534, is recorded.
